consequence: Query expansion does not enter the grounded pipeline. Nothing is wired. The module and the tools stay in the repository as measured, experimental code. BLIND TEST-2 is a USED HOLDOUT from this run on. The embedding / semantic re-ranker option goes to the Owner as a decision.
ceiling: not applicable: the baseline hit 12 of 25 strict probes, far below the ceiling clause (23)
reading: The gain is real but small and did not generalise at the size seen on DEV (DEV +4 / 0, TEST-2 +3 / -1). With 3 gains and 1 regression a one-sided sign test gives p = 0.31: no evidence.

All three gains came from the expansion slot, two of them for passages that were not within the first 200 of the lexical ranking at all - the mechanism does what it was built for, just not often enough.
The one regression is the predicted cost of SLOTS with keep 4: the passage that answers was 5th in the original result and lost its place to the expansion slot.
Of the 11 probes missed by both, 8 had a valid expansion and were still missed: the limit is not only the discarded expansions.

9 of the 10 discarded expansions stated a number the question did not contain - on 'how often / how long / how much' questions the model answers instead of rewriting. The check did its job; it also means the mechanism is weakest exactly where a precise passage matters most.
The more important number is the baseline on unseen strict probes: 12 of 25 (48 %). probes-v1 had suggested 9 of 14. Lexical retrieval over this library is weaker than Phase 4.8 showed.
